answer: For agents financing ferrous surveys in the tundra, require every loan to reserve collateral worth more than its principal in a shared escrow registry. Each pledge references an unspent asset ID, so aliases cannot borrow against the same deposit repeatedly. A hollow web of new accounts adds no borrowing capacity: another loan needs more locked capital. Liquidate collateral when repayment fails and apply a haircut for price swings. This blocks identity-reset credit theft, provided asset custody and valuation are independently checked.
